rationale: A levelling sight must present a known axis, and the object marks one. NOTE: C-17 IS THE FIRST CANDIDATE SCORED ON EV046, which was added after every hypothesis had been specified. This advantages it relative to H001-H014, all of which are silent on the variable
A through-sight needs truly circular apertures at both ends
Thin walls give a sharper sight; a thick wall makes a tube
Optical use; nothing passes through, so the absence of bore wear counts in favour
The readings are angles; departure from regular geometry is direct instrument error, and EXP-0004 shows the margin is already too thin to absorb any
A level must give the same reading in any workman's hands. The corpus varies 2.5:1 in size and its pair differences, which set the precision, vary from 0.3 to 10.2 mm between specimens
Suspension from a cord is required by the mechanism and must bear on the object
Predicts urban and engineering contexts, which the corpus shows
Predicts association with surveying or levelling equipment - a chorobates, dioptra, groma, libra, or a plumb bob. None is recorded with any dodecahedron

Aqueducts were built across the whole empire, and most spectacularly in Italy, Africa and the East. An instrument for building them had no reason to stay in the north-western provinces; the confinement is present
A shadowless disc is a null reading and needs truly circular apertures at both ends of the sight line
Thin walls give a sharper null; a thick wall turns the aperture into a tube and blurs the alignment
Optical use; nothing passes through, so the absence of bore wear counts in favour

THE CANDIDATE'S DISTINCTIVE STRENGTH. The face-axis angles are fixed by the polyhedron and are identical in a 40 mm and a 100 mm specimen, so the instrument needs no standardisation at all. It is the only proposal in the project for which the absence of a standard is predicted rather than merely tolerated
The readings ARE angles, so departure from regular geometry is direct instrument error

NEUTRAL, AND A DEBIT RATHER THAN A DODGE: the mechanism does not need graded apertures at all. Aperture size affects only the tolerance of the null, not which elevation is read. The candidate leaves the single strongest feature of the corpus unexplained
Opposite apertures should be near-matched, since their difference sets the angular tolerance of the null: about 1 to 3 degrees for the observed 2 to 4.5 mm pair differences over a 50 mm path
Repeated suspension from a cord must bear on the knob and leave rope wear
The suspension cord bears directly on whichever knob is used
Clean aperture edges are needed for a sharp null
Predicts urban and domestic contexts, which the corpus shows
Predicts association with calendrical or astronomical equipment; none is recorded with any dodecahedron

EXP-0003 shows the four noon-reachable elevations are identical from 43.7 to 55 degrees north, so the instrument is latitude-insensitive across the empire and had no reason to remain in the north-western provinces. Confinement therefore counts against it
Twelve apertures for twelve zodiac months is the functional claim
A dial reads angles. Geometric fidelity is the whole instrument, and EXP-0002 shows irregularity degrades the resolution further
A dial is calibrated for one latitude and must be reproducible; the corpus spans 43 to 55 degrees north with no systematic geometric variation and no standardisation at all
A dial must be oriented to the meridian and held fixed. No specimen has a base, a suspension loop or any distinguished axis; the knobs let it rest on any face
The interior IS the projection surface. It must be smoothed and it must carry engraved declination curves, as every Roman zodiac dial does. The corpus interiors are rough, unfinished and unmarked

The interior is the projection surface and must be smooth and true. The PAS records in this database consistently describe interiors as roughly or crudely cast and unfinished (RD-0001, RD-0002, RD-0003, RD-0008, RD-0011, RD-0012)

Every Roman zodiac dial carries engraved declination curves ON THE PROJECTION SURFACE. The engraving on these objects is entirely on the EXTERIOR, around the apertures; no specimen has interior markings
Optical use; nothing passes through the apertures, so the absence of bore wear counts in favour
Predicts urban and domestic contexts, which the corpus shows
Predicts association with other timekeeping or astronomical equipment. None is recorded with any dodecahedron

A latitude-calibrated instrument would be confined to a band of latitudes, which is the one argument in this candidate's favour. WEAK: the corpus spans 43 to 55 degrees north, some 12 degrees, which is far too wide for a single calibration
A graded set of apertures IS a graded set of garment sizes. This is the whole functional claim
A gauge aperture must be truly circular or the size it reports is wrong
The lip must be rounded, because cloth or leather is drawn against it and a sharp rim would snag or cut the work
Only soft material passes the aperture, and briefly. Absence of bore wear counts in favour. NOTE this is the same premise as C-12 and it was chosen knowing the wear result
A casting flaw on a working aperture distorts the size it reports
Engraved rings around an aperture could serve to identify which size it is, which a graded set needs
A gauge carries no load; thin walls suffice

NEUTRAL, AND THIS IS THE CANDIDATE'S WEAK POINT RATHER THAN A DODGE: a sizing gauge does not need knobs at all, let alone twenty of them. The hypothesis leaves the most distinctive feature of the object unexplained, which is exactly what H014 and C-12 do explain

NEUTRAL: each aperture is independently a gauge, so overall regularity of the body is irrelevant. This is a genuine indifference and is what separates C-13 from C-11, where the references are relations BETWEEN knobs and global regularity does matter
A workshop gauge need only be self-consistent to make matched pairs, so standardisation between objects is expected but not required. Predicted at '+' rather than '++' for that reason
Predicts urban workshop and domestic contexts, which the corpus shows

Garment forms were regionally specific in a way that artillery and fishing were not. The north-western provinces had a distinctive and high-value textile tradition: the birrus Britannicus is named in Diocletian's Price Edict of AD 301, mid-window, at 6,000 denarii, and hooded garments are a Gallic and north-western style (PUB-0043). A tool for a regionally specific garment may legitimately be regionally confined
Predicts needles, shears, thimbles, awls, spindle whorls, loom weights or cloth alongside. None is recorded with any dodecahedron
Regional garment traditions imply regionally varying tools
Textile or leather fibres should remain against the aperture lips
A distance or angle gauge that varies between objects transfers no measurement. DECISIVE: overall diameter varies 2.5:1 across the corpus
Inter-knob distances must be predictable from the form; an irregular body gives unpredictable references
Casting distortion displaces the reference points and corrupts every measurement taken from them
The reference points must be uniform in size and placement
Knob diameter must be consistent or the contact point shifts
Nothing passes through the apertures; absence of bore wear counts in favour, as it does for H011
Predicts urban, architectural and workshop contexts, which the corpus shows
Predicts association with surveying or drafting equipment - groma, dividers, rules, styli. None is recorded with any dodecahedron
Measurement practice was empire-wide; confinement to the north-west would falsify, and the confinement is present

THE UNIFYING PREMISE. Nothing harder than bronze ever contacts the tool, so no bore wear can form. All four wear predictions below follow deductively from this one premise rather than being chosen separately
Soft material cannot abrade the exterior
No cord is drawn under tension across the object
Nothing rotates against the object
Graded apertures suit different work sizes
The knobs are standoffs that set the thickness of the formed piece
Standoffs must be uniform or thickness varies across the work
The tool carries no structural load; thin walls suffice
Relief around an aperture impresses itself into soft material, which makes the decoration a working surface rather than ornament
Engraving after casting creates that impressing surface
A craft tool need not conform to any standard; the gauge wanted varies with the work
Craft traditions and their tools vary by region
Predicts workshop and urban domestic contexts, which the corpus shows
A regionally transmitted craft may be regionally confined. WEAK: almost any culturally specific explanation predicts this

Predicts craft equipment alongside - awls, punches, offcuts, scrap foil, raw material. None is recorded with any dodecahedron. THIS IS THE CANDIDATE'S ONLY HARD CONTRADICTION and it is the same one that costs H014 its largest single loss
Residues of whatever was worked should remain on the interior and around the apertures. THE DECISIVE AND UNMEASURED TEST
A gauge that is not standardised sorts nothing; two gauges must agree
Stone or lead shot dragged through bronze apertures abrades them
A gauge handled with shot must be robust
Aperture geometry must be true or the calibration is wrong
Predicts military dominance; corpus is more than half urban settlement and under one-fifth military (PUB-0003, 33)
Artillery served empire-wide; confinement to the north-west would falsify. The confinement is present (PUB-0003, 32)
Predicts shot, artillery fittings or military kit alongside; none is recorded with any dodecahedron
Straps and traces under draught tension bear on the fitting constantly
Anything routed through an aperture under draught load wears the bore
A draught fitting carries real load and must be substantial
Must not deform under harness tension
Harness parts are replaced and must interchange
Predicts military and rural dominance; the corpus is urban civilian
Predicts harness fittings, bits or vehicle parts alongside; none is recorded
A mesh gauge that varies between objects produces unusable netting
Cord is drawn round the gauge under tension at every mesh
Cord bearing on the knobs at every mesh must wear them
Fishing and fowling are practised across the empire; confinement to the north-west would falsify, and the confinement is present
Predicts coastal, riverine and lacustrine sites; the corpus is inland urban settlement
Predicts net weights, floats or hooks alongside; none is recorded
A fairlead exists to take rope load; rope wear is its defining trace
Rope running through an aperture under load grooves the bore
Rigging loads are large; thin walls would collapse
Must transfer load between rope and hull or spar
Predicts ports, wrecks and riverine sites; the corpus is inland urban
Shipping is Mediterranean above all; absence from Italy, Spain, Africa and the East falsifies
A measure that is not standardised measures nothing. THIS IS DECISIVE: overall diameter varies 2.5:1 across the corpus
Internal volume must be true and reproducible
Casting voids alter internal volume and would be rejected
Apertures perforating the vessel make it unable to hold anything measurable. THIS ALONE ELIMINATES THE CANDIDATE
Roman measures were empire-wide; regional confinement falsifies
Pressed into soil repeatedly; abrasive wear is unavoidable
Contact with stones in tilled soil chips and dents
Spacing must be reproducible between tools
Predicts rural and agricultural contexts; the corpus is urban settlement
A tool pressed into soil must be robust; the corpus is 0.5-4 mm
A clapper striking the interior leaves impact traces around the apertures and inside
A bell on a beast is knocked constantly
Suspension from a collar or strap wears the suspension point
Constant contact with hide, vegetation and other stock
Predicts rural and pastoral contexts; the corpus is urban settlement
A hung bell has a fixed orientation and needs a suspension loop; no dodecahedron has one
A tether point exists to take rope load under an animal's pull
Rope through an aperture under an animal's weight grooves the bore
Must resist the pull of a large animal; 0.5-4 mm of leaded bronze would not
Must not deform or burst under shock loading
Predicts rural, pastoral and military-transport contexts

Combustion residues should remain on the interior
Handled and hung in use
